questions.prompt: What role does a new interpretation of struggles have in this passage?
questions.promptZh: 本段中，对挣扎的新解释起什么作用？
options: It guarantees every difficult event is erased from history.
It forms a foundational step towards self-understanding and further transformation.
It replaces all actual experience with money or possessions.
It proves that past struggles never happened.
optionsZh: 保证每件困难事件从历史消失。
成为自我理解与进一步转变的基础一步。
用金钱财物替换全部真实经历。
证明过去困难从未发生。
analyses: A 新解释不是抹去已发生事件，后文还明确不删掉全部坏经历。
B becomes a foundational step toward后的两个方向均保留。
C 原句谈interpretation，不是财物替代。
D struggles被承认为解释对象，不是原句证明其不存在；基础一步也非所有结果立刻实现的保证。

vocabulary.meaning: 基础性的；为后续发展提供支撑的
vocabulary.context: 修饰step，强调过程的一步，不是全部转变都已完成。
vocabulary.example: The new interpretation became a foundational step in her understanding.

questions.evidenceQuote: You can see your struggles from a different perspective, and the new interpretation of those struggles becomes a foundational step toward self-understanding and further transformation. Edit your story, drop the old version of yourself, and come to believe in the new version of your narrative. I am not saying that you should edit out all the bad experiences to create a happier version of your life story. Not at all.

questions.prompt: Which reading of 'drop the old version' fits the following clarification?
questions.promptZh: 怎样理解 drop the old version 才符合后面的澄清？
options: Revise one's self-narrative without assuming all bad experiences must be deleted.
Remove every bad event from the story so that nothing painful remains.
Deny that the original experiences occurred at all.
Treat the new version as a guarantee that all external circumstances have changed.
optionsZh: 更新自我叙述，不因此认定必须删掉所有坏经历。
把每个坏事件都删去，不留痛苦。
否认原有经历曾发生。
把新版叙述当作外部一切处境已改变的保证。
analyses: A 前句是叙述更新，后句I am not saying...edit out all bad experiences限定其含义。
B 正是作者明确否认的删法。
C 编辑解释与否认事实不同。
D believe in new narrative是叙述更新，不是外部一切处境已改变的实测保证。

vocabulary.meaning: 叙述；以某种结构和视角讲述经历的故事
vocabulary.context: 版本可改变的是自我理解与呈现，不是自动逆转已发生历史。
vocabulary.example: She reconsidered the narrative she had built around the event.
collocations: the new version of your narrative

questions.evidenceQuote: You can see your struggles from a different perspective, and the new interpretation of those struggles becomes a foundational step toward self-understanding and further transformation. Edit your story, drop the old version of yourself, and come to believe in the new version of your narrative. I am not saying that you should edit out all the bad experiences to create a happier version of your life story. Not at all.

questions.prompt: What condition underlies the offered example of making experiences more interesting?
questions.promptZh: 让经历更有意思的例子基于什么条件？
options: The person has never had any experience to draw on.
The author says every event must be invented rather than remembered.
The person must have earned more money than every other person.
The person has had unusual experiences or difficult periods that can be reinterpreted.
optionsZh: 此人没有任何可依据的经历。
作者说每件事必须编造而非记忆。
此人必须比其他每人赚更多钱。
此人曾有不寻常经历或艰难时期，可重新理解讲述。
analyses: A if you’ve had明确以前已有经历，非全无。
B edit them回指经历，不是必须虚构。
C interesting与赚钱排名无关，本句未设收入条件。
D if条件与could可能性均保留，例子有地震、飓风、艰难时期，不是鼓励主动寻求灾难。

vocabulary.meaning: 艰难时期；生活中困难的一段时间
vocabulary.context: 与地震飓风并列为已有经历例，不是要求每个人都遭同样事件。
vocabulary.example: The account included tough periods as well as successes.
collocations: make them more interesting to you and others

questions.evidenceQuote: You can’t make an uneventful life psychologically rich. I bet even Virginia Woolf couldn’t. But if you’ve had some unusual experiences such as an earthquake or hurricane or tough periods in your life, you could edit them to make them more interesting to you and others. That will then become part of your story and who you are.

questions.prompt: What does the edited account become part of, according to the next sentence?
questions.promptZh: 按下一句，编辑后的叙述会成为哪部分？
options: Only the official disaster record and no part of personal identity.
Only the publisher's list of sales figures.
The person's story and sense of who they are.
A proof that every person must tell exactly the same story.
optionsZh: 只成官方灾难档案，与个人认同无关。
只成出版社销量清单。
个人故事及其自我身份认知的一部分。
证明每个人必须讲完全一样的故事。
analyses: A who you are正把叙述联系到自我，不是排除。
B 无出版销售资料。
C That承接重新编辑已有经历，your story与who you are两个落点均在句中。
D 个人叙述进入身份不要求各人内容完全相同。

vocabulary.meaning: 你是谁；这里指个人身份与自我理解
vocabulary.context: 不是只问姓名、证件号码或把叙述变成法定身份修改。
vocabulary.example: The story became part of how she understood who she was.
collocations: part of your story and who you are

questions.evidenceQuote: You can’t make an uneventful life psychologically rich. I bet even Virginia Woolf couldn’t. But if you’ve had some unusual experiences such as an earthquake or hurricane or tough periods in your life, you could edit them to make them more interesting to you and others. That will then become part of your story and who you are.

questions.prompt: What does the 'unless' sentence claim is necessary for a psychologically rich life?
questions.promptZh: unless句声称心理丰富人生需要什么？
options: A life containing interesting experiences, rather than wording alone without experience.
A guarantee that every experience is pleasant and painless.
A requirement to publish a book before having any experience.
The absence of all unusual experiences or challenges.
optionsZh: 人生中有有趣经历，而非无经历只改措辞。
保证每次体验都愉快无痛。
必须先出版一本书才能有经历。
没有任何不寻常经历或挑战。
analyses: A Unless...not going to be将有趣经历置于必要背景，前句experience itself也明确。
B interesting并不等于pleasant，作者多次承认不快乐的丰富经历。
C 未要求出版，story editor是讲述比喻。
D 与full of interesting experiences方向相反；保持这是作者的论述，不把一句条件命题当量化生活诊断。

vocabulary.meaning: 除非；若没有这个条件则……
vocabulary.context: 与not搭配表达缺少有趣经历时的否定，不应漏读成只靠讲法就足够。
vocabulary.example: Unless the account draws on experience, vivid wording alone may not suffice.
collocations: Unless you have a life full of interesting experiences
not going to be a psychologically rich one

questions.evidenceQuote: At the heart of a psychologically rich life is experience itself. Unless you have a life full of interesting experiences, it is not going to be a psychologically rich one. But if you become a better “story editor,” you can extract the most interesting aspects of your experiences and make your story psychologically richer. Another benefit of story editing is that the well-edited story is easier to remember.

questions.prompt: What can a better 'story editor' extract from experience?
questions.promptZh: 更好的story editor能从经历中提取什么？
options: Events that never took place and must replace all actual memories.
Only the financial value of damaged property.
A guarantee that every remembered detail is objectively perfect.
The most interesting aspects of experiences, making the story psychologically richer.
optionsZh: 从未发生且必须替换一切真实记忆的事件。
只有受损财物的经济价值。
保证每个回忆细节客观完美。
经历最有意思的方面，使故事心理上更丰富。
analyses: A your experiences限定已有素材，不是要求造假替换。
B 这不是财物估价任务。
C extract interesting aspects并不验证全部记忆细节。
D if you become...can extract明确能力条件与提取内容，richer描述故事呈现，不偷换成实际多经历过新事件。

vocabulary.meaning: 提取；从材料中找出并突出某些方面
vocabulary.context: 此处为选择和阐释经历的有趣点，不是无中生有。
vocabulary.example: The writer extracted the most interesting aspects of the experience.

questions.evidenceQuote: At the heart of a psychologically rich life is experience itself. Unless you have a life full of interesting experiences, it is not going to be a psychologically rich one. But if you become a better “story editor,” you can extract the most interesting aspects of your experiences and make your story psychologically richer. Another benefit of story editing is that the well-edited story is easier to remember.

questions.prompt: How does the passage define the narrative identity studied by McAdams?
questions.promptZh: 原文怎样解释McAdams研究的narrative identity？
options: Only a person's official name and passport number.
How people tell their life stories, studied using the Life Story Interview.
The number of novels a person sells to a publisher.
A genetic test that replaces interviews about experience.
optionsZh: 仅一个人的法定姓名及护照号码。
人怎样讲人生故事，以Life Story Interview研究。
一个人卖给出版社的小说数量。
取代经历访谈的基因测验。
analyses: A or后明确是讲人生，不是身份证件。
B 定义与using a method called两项完整对应。
C 书或小说是访谈比喻，不是销量指标。
D 本句研究方法是访谈，不是基因检测；last forty years是原书叙述的时间背景，不改成网站当前累积年数。

vocabulary.meaning: 叙事认同；通过讲述人生形成的自我理解
vocabulary.context: 按本句or how people tell...解释，非仅户籍身份。
vocabulary.example: The interview explored narrative identity through a person's life story.

questions.evidenceQuote: Over the last forty years, the psychologist Dan McAdams has studied “narrative identity,” or how people tell their life stories, using a method called the “Life Story Interview.” An interview begins with this prompt: “Please begin by thinking about your life as if it were a book or novel. Imagine that the book has a table of contents containing the titles of the main chapters in the story. To begin here, please describe very briefly what the main chapters in the book might be.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of imagining a table of contents?
questions.promptZh: 想象一份目录的目的是什么？
options: To recite this study book's real chapter titles from memory.
To require publication of an actual novel before answering any interview question.
To organise one's life story into main chapters or periods.
To count the interviewer's academic articles instead of personal experience.
optionsZh: 背诵本学习书真实章名。
要求回答任何访谈题前先出版真实小说。
把自己的人生故事组织为主要章节或阶段。
统计访谈者论文而非自己的经历。
analyses: A as if your life were book说明对象是受访者人生，不是本书目录。
B Imagine的比喻提示不等于现实出版前提。
C main chapters in the story让人梳理人生阶段，是访谈开头的结构化引导。
D 目录内容是life story，非研究者论文清单；as if与Imagine共同表明这是组织人生叙述的比喻。

vocabulary.meaning: 目录；列出主要章节标题的结构
vocabulary.context: 在此为人生分段的比喻，不是要把书中章名复制成每个人人生。
vocabulary.example: She imagined a table of contents for the major periods of her life.
collocations: a table of contents containing the titles
the main chapters in the story

questions.evidenceQuote: Over the last forty years, the psychologist Dan McAdams has studied “narrative identity,” or how people tell their life stories, using a method called the “Life Story Interview.” An interview begins with this prompt: “Please begin by thinking about your life as if it were a book or novel. Imagine that the book has a table of contents containing the titles of the main chapters in the story. To begin here, please describe very briefly what the main chapters in the book might be.

questions.prompt: Which kind of key scene does the 'low point' prompt seek?
questions.promptZh: low point提示要找哪类关键场景？
options: A particularly difficult or unhappy episode in the life story.
Only the proudest success or happiest moment.
Only the next planned career move in the future.
The final summary theme instead of any episode.
optionsZh: 人生故事中特别困难或不快乐的经历。
只有最骄傲成功或最快乐时刻。
只有未来计划的下一次职业行动。
不谈经历，只给最终总结主题。
analyses: A low point在关键场景清单中指低谷，与high point相对。
B 这是high point而非low point。
C 后文另有future问题，不能把过去低谷换成未来计划。
D 当前问一个场景，不是访谈最后提炼主题的步骤。

vocabulary.meaning: 低谷；最艰难、最失落的时刻或阶段
vocabulary.context: 这里是人生场景意义，不是海拔最低的地点。
vocabulary.example: The interview asked about a low point as well as a high point.

questions.evidenceQuote: Once the interviewee answers these questions, they are asked to think of a few key scenes that stand out in their story: What was the high point of your life? What was the low point? What was the turning point? Can you name a positive childhood memory?

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a turning point from merely a high or low point?
questions.promptZh: turning point 与单纯高点或低点有何区别？
options: It must be the happiest event without changing anything.
It must describe only a childhood memory with no later effect.
It is an exact midpoint in age, regardless of what happened.
It marks a change in the direction of the person's story.
optionsZh: 必定是最快乐且没有改变任何事的事件。
必只讲毫无后续影响的童年记忆。
不论事件，都是年龄的准确中点。
它标志故事发展方向发生变化。
analyses: A 转折不要求最快乐，重点不只是情绪高低。
B 童年只是另一提示类别，不是turning point的排他定义。
C point不是精确年龄算术中点。
D 关键场景中的turning强调改变走向，既不预设好转，也不必一定变坏。

vocabulary.meaning: 转折点；使后续发展方向改变的重要事件或阶段
vocabulary.context: 区别high/low的情绪评价，并不预设转向一定积极。
vocabulary.example: She described the move as a turning point in her story.

questions.evidenceQuote: Once the interviewee answers these questions, they are asked to think of a few key scenes that stand out in their story: What was the high point of your life? What was the low point? What was the turning point? Can you name a positive childhood memory?

questions.prompt: Which memory specifically fits the childhood prompt in this extract?
questions.promptZh: 哪种记忆符合当前片段的童年提示？
options: A hoped-for retirement trip that has not occurred.
A positive memory from childhood.
Only a negative episode from an adult career.
An anonymous stranger's future career plan.
optionsZh: 尚未发生的退休旅行愿望。
一段积极的童年记忆。
只有成年职业中的负面经历。
匿名陌生人的未来职业计划。
analyses: A memory指已过往，childhood也不是退休未来。
B positive、childhood、memory三个限制均匹配。
C 情绪性质、人生阶段都与本提示不同。
D 访谈讨论受访者自己的过往故事，不是陌生人的未来计划。

vocabulary.meaning: 积极的；这里指带有良好情感的回忆性质
vocabulary.context: 与childhood搭配限定记忆，不是考试正确选项标签或数学正数。
vocabulary.example: The prompt asked for a positive childhood memory.

questions.evidenceQuote: Once the interviewee answers these questions, they are asked to think of a few key scenes that stand out in their story: What was the high point of your life? What was the low point? What was the turning point? Can you name a positive childhood memory?

questions.prompt: What part of the interview do dreams, hopes, and plans belong to?
questions.promptZh: dreams、hopes、plans属于访谈哪一部分？
options: Only a count of published chapters in the researcher's textbook.
A test proving every childhood recollection is accurate.
Imagining the interviewee's future, rather than reporting only completed past events.
A requirement that every future plan has already succeeded.
optionsZh: 只统计研究者教材已出版章数。
证明每个童年回忆准确的测验。
想象受访者未来，而非只报告已完成的过去事件。
要求每个未来计划都已经成功。
analyses: A 对象是their future，不是研究书目。
B 这里转到未来提问，不是回忆准确性试验。
C 开头imagine their future明确问题阶段，梦想希望计划均可尚未实现。
D plans不是已实现结果，原文也未要求全部计划都已成功。

vocabulary.meaning: 希望；对未来的期盼
vocabulary.context: 与dreams和plans并列，不自动等于可确认的将来结果。
vocabulary.example: The interview moved from past scenes to hopes for the future.

questions.evidenceQuote: Then the interviewee is asked to imagine their future: What is the next chapter of your life? What are your dreams, hopes, and plans? Then there are questions about challenges, religious and political ideology, and values. Finally, the interviewee is asked to reflect upon their life story and extract a main theme.

questions.prompt: How are redemption and contamination narratives positioned in the classification?
questions.promptZh: 救赎叙事与污染叙事在分类中处于什么位置？
options: They are two main types within many possible ways of classifying narratives.
They are the only two types any story could possibly have, with no other classification allowed.
They are two laboratory diagnoses applied to every interviewee.
They describe only how many chapters a printed novel has.
optionsZh: 它们是在多种可能分类方式中的两个主要类型。
它们是所有故事唯一可能类型，不允许其他分类。
它们是用于每位受访者的两种实验室诊断。
它们只描述印刷小说有多少章。
analyses: A many ways与two main types两部分都保留。
B main不是only possible，不能删去many ways。
C narrative类型不是临床或实验室诊断。
D 这里讨论叙事发展方式，非仅目录计数。

vocabulary.meaning: 分类；按某种特征分成类别
vocabulary.context: 这里承认有多种分类框架，不把两个主要原型当作所有故事无例外的排他归宿。
vocabulary.example: Researchers can classify narratives in more than one way.

questions.evidenceQuote: There are many ways to classify narratives, but two main types are the redemption narrative and the contamination narrative. George W. Bush’s story is a typical redemption narrative that goes from good to bad before it hits a turning point and concludes with a happy ending. G.W.’s story was so prototypical that McAdams even wrote a book entitled George W. Bush and the Redemptive Dream. The other archetype is a contamination narrative, where people tell a story that starts out good but goes south after a certain point.

questions.prompt: Why is McAdams's book about G.W. mentioned?
questions.promptZh: 为何提及McAdams关于G.W.的那本书？
options: To prove G.W. conducted the Life Story Interview himself.
To identify the only story that has ever been told about a politician.
To say the book rejects all analysis of redemption narratives.
To illustrate how prototypical G.W.'s story was as a redemption narrative.
optionsZh: 证明G.W.本人开展人生故事访谈。
认定历史上关于政治人物只讲过这一个故事。
说该书拒绝一切救赎叙事分析。
说明G.W.故事作为救赎叙事有多典型。
analyses: A 作者是McAdams，非由G.W.开展该访谈的证据。
B 提一本书不等于政治叙事仅此一例。
C 前句典型redemption与书名Redemptive Dream同向，非拒绝。
D so prototypical that...even wrote构成典型程度的例证；不把作者所选叙事框架当对人物一生的唯一事实版本。

vocabulary.meaning: 典型的；充分体现某一类型特征的
vocabulary.context: 指故事符合所述原型，不表示每个相关事实都经此句独立核实。
vocabulary.example: The account was presented as a prototypical redemption narrative.
collocations: George W. Bush and the Redemptive Dream

questions.evidenceQuote: There are many ways to classify narratives, but two main types are the redemption narrative and the contamination narrative. George W. Bush’s story is a typical redemption narrative that goes from good to bad before it hits a turning point and concludes with a happy ending. G.W.’s story was so prototypical that McAdams even wrote a book entitled George W. Bush and the Redemptive Dream. The other archetype is a contamination narrative, where people tell a story that starts out good but goes south after a certain point.

questions.prompt: What does 'goes south' mean in the contamination narrative?
questions.promptZh: 污染叙事里的 goes south 是什么意思？
options: The characters must travel to a southern country.
The story begins well but turns for the worse after a certain point.
Every story ends happily after all difficulties disappear.
The narrator changes only the font used in the title.
optionsZh: 人物必须去南方国家。
故事开头良好，但某节点后变糟。
每个故事在困难全消后快乐收尾。
叙述者仅改标题字体。
analyses: A goes south在这里是变差习语，不是地理移动要求。
B starts out good与but...after a certain point给由好转坏方向。
C 与污染叙事走向相反，混入救赎式结局。
D 这里说情节发展，不是排版改变。

vocabulary.meaning: 变糟；朝不利方向发展
vocabulary.context: 在叙事语境中说明情节转坏，不是实际向南行。
vocabulary.example: The account begins happily but goes south after a setback.
collocations: starts out good but goes south

questions.evidenceQuote: There are many ways to classify narratives, but two main types are the redemption narrative and the contamination narrative. George W. Bush’s story is a typical redemption narrative that goes from good to bad before it hits a turning point and concludes with a happy ending. G.W.’s story was so prototypical that McAdams even wrote a book entitled George W. Bush and the Redemptive Dream. The other archetype is a contamination narrative, where people tell a story that starts out good but goes south after a certain point.

questions.prompt: What kind of relationship is stated between narrative identity and personality?
questions.promptZh: 叙事认同与人格之间被表述为哪种关系？
options: They are declared completely unrelated in every case.
Narrative identity is defined as an official medical diagnosis.
Narrative identity is associated with various personality traits.
A single story is said to prove the fixed cause of every trait for every person.
optionsZh: 被断言在任何情况都完全无关。
叙事认同被定义为正式医学诊断。
叙事认同与多种人格特质有关联。
说一个故事能证明每人每项特质的固定成因。
analyses: A associated with与完全无关相反。
B or how we tell life stories是定义，非医学诊断。
C various traits与associated两项保留。
D 关联不等于对所有人确证同一因果，更不能凭单个故事诊断全部人格。

vocabulary.meaning: 与……有关联
vocabulary.context: 这里是叙述方式与特质之间的关系，不独自确定因果方向。
vocabulary.example: Narrative tone was associated with several self-reported traits.

questions.evidenceQuote: Narrative identity, or how we tell our life stories, is associated with various personality traits. For example, individuals who tell a redemptive story report themselves to be more conscientious, agreeable, extraverted, and less neurotic than those who do not. The emotional tone of a life narrative is more positive among agreeable, conscientious, and non-neurotic people than among disagreeable, unconscientious, and neurotic people. Individuals high in openness to experience tend to tell more complex stories than those low in openness.

questions.prompt: Which self-reported pattern is linked with telling a redemptive story?
questions.promptZh: 讲救赎故事与哪种自报特质模式相联系？
options: More conscientious, agreeable, and extraverted, and less neurotic.
Less conscientious, less agreeable, less extraverted, and more neurotic.
Only higher openness, with every other trait explicitly identical.
Identical measured traits for all people regardless of story type.
optionsZh: 更尽责、更宜人、更外向，且较低神经质。
较不尽责、较不宜人、较不外向，且更高神经质。
只有开放性高，明确说其余特质完全相同。
无论故事类型，每人实测特质完全一致。
analyses: A more三项与less neurotic逐项对应，保留report themselves为自报。
B 四方向都反了。
C 开放性与复杂性为同段另一关系，不是本句的唯一模式。
D 原文给比较方向，并非所有人的客观测量同值；特质用语不是给读者或叙述者贴疾病诊断。

vocabulary.meaning: 尽责的；认真负责、做事有条理的
vocabulary.context: 人格特质用语，不能混成conscious清醒的，也不由故事类型单独决定。
vocabulary.example: The participants described themselves as conscientious.

questions.evidenceQuote: Narrative identity, or how we tell our life stories, is associated with various personality traits. For example, individuals who tell a redemptive story report themselves to be more conscientious, agreeable, extraverted, and less neurotic than those who do not. The emotional tone of a life narrative is more positive among agreeable, conscientious, and non-neurotic people than among disagreeable, unconscientious, and neurotic people. Individuals high in openness to experience tend to tell more complex stories than those low in openness.

questions.prompt: Among whom is life-narrative tone described as more positive?
questions.promptZh: 文中说哪类人的人生叙事情绪基调更积极？
options: Disagreeable, unconscientious, and neurotic people compared with the opposite pattern.
Every person has the same narrative tone regardless of traits.
Only people with no memories of difficult events.
Agreeable, conscientious, and non-neurotic people compared with the contrasting traits.
optionsZh: 不宜人、不尽责、高神经质者，相比相反特质者。
每人叙事基调都相同，与特质无关。
只有完全没有困难记忆的人。
宜人、尽责、低神经质者，相比相反特质者。
analyses: A 将两组与more positive的方向交换。
B more positive among...than...明确有差异。
C 未说必须没有困难经历，积极基调不等于从无损失。
D 两组三项及比较方向都保留；more positive不是人人始终正面或所有事件本身幸福。

vocabulary.meaning: 情绪基调；叙述整体呈现的情感色彩
vocabulary.context: 区分故事如何讲与每个事件本身是否快乐，也非某一次瞬时情绪得分。
vocabulary.example: The emotional tone of the narrative was positive despite the setbacks.
collocations: The emotional tone of a life narrative

questions.evidenceQuote: Narrative identity, or how we tell our life stories, is associated with various personality traits. For example, individuals who tell a redemptive story report themselves to be more conscientious, agreeable, extraverted, and less neurotic than those who do not. The emotional tone of a life narrative is more positive among agreeable, conscientious, and non-neurotic people than among disagreeable, unconscientious, and neurotic people. Individuals high in openness to experience tend to tell more complex stories than those low in openness.

questions.prompt: What does the opening of the perspective study claim changes?
questions.promptZh: 视角研究开头说什么会发生变化？
options: Past events themselves are physically replaced by new events.
The way people tell a life story can change with its perspective.
All participants acquire identical personalities after one question.
The book gives a fixed price for every life story.
optionsZh: 过去事件本身被实际换成新事件。
讲人生故事的方式可随叙述视角而变。
每位参与者一题之后人格完全一样。
本书给每个人生故事固定价格。
analyses: A changes the way tell不等于改写已发生历史。
B perspective与way people tell构成此处关系，后面的两组提问用于说明。
C 没有全员人格同化结果。
D 未测故事价格；Recent studies是相对原书写作的表述，不冒充网站新检索的最新研究。

vocabulary.meaning: 视角；看待或组织叙述的角度
vocabulary.context: 在此关于故事讲法，不仅是眼睛站在何处的物理位置。
vocabulary.example: A change in perspective altered how the same story was told.
collocations: the perspective of a life story
changes the way people tell it

questions.evidenceQuote: Recent studies also show that the perspective of a life story changes the way people tell it. For instance, Benjamin Rogers and colleagues asked half of a group of participants a series of questions such as: “What makes you you?” “What change of setting or novel experience prompted your journey to become who you are today?” “What overall goal were you striving for that led to who you are today?”

questions.prompt: What does the prompt 'What makes you you?' ask participants to consider?
questions.promptZh: What makes you you? 提示参与者思考什么？
options: Only the exact spelling of their legal name.
Only the number of rooms in the research laboratory.
The features or experiences that define who they are.
A compulsory requirement to adopt the researcher's identity.
optionsZh: 只想法定姓名的准确拼写。
只想研究实验室房间数。
使其成为其自身的特征或经历。
必须采用研究者身份。
analyses: A 两个you的结构在此探问身份形成，不只拼姓名。
B 与后续旅程、环境、目标等提示无关。
C 问自身成为自身的缘由，放在Rogers团队的旅程式提问中理解。
D 反思自己不等于变成研究者；half说明这是一组条件，不是所有人都收同样问题。

vocabulary.meaning: 一系列问题；相互衔接的多项提问
vocabulary.context: 当前提示是其中例子，不等于单个姓名登记栏或所有研究条件完全相同。
vocabulary.example: The interview used a series of questions about identity and experience.
collocations: asked half of a group of participants
a series of questions such as

questions.evidenceQuote: Recent studies also show that the perspective of a life story changes the way people tell it. For instance, Benjamin Rogers and colleagues asked half of a group of participants a series of questions such as: “What makes you you?” “What change of setting or novel experience prompted your journey to become who you are today?” “What overall goal were you striving for that led to who you are today?”

questions.prompt: Which part of a person's journey does the challenge prompt focus on?
questions.promptZh: 有关挑战的提示聚焦个人历程哪一部分？
options: Obstacles, rivals, or negative events that stood in the way.
Only the rewards received after every difficulty vanished.
Only neutral features of work and home with no obstacle.
Proof that every person literally has the same named enemy.
optionsZh: 阻路的障碍、竞争者或负面事件。
只有所有困难消失后的奖励。
只有工作住家的中性特征，不谈障碍。
证明每人真的有同一个有名宿敌。
analyses: A challenges or obstacles与such as例子和stood in way直接对应。
B 问阻碍，不只事后奖励。
C mundane工作住家是另一条件的提问，不是本项。
D such as给可选示例，不要求每人实际都有同一个或任何一个宿敌。

vocabulary.meaning: 阻挡；妨碍达到某方向或目标
vocabulary.context: 旅程比喻中指困难与阻力，不是必须有人站在路中央。
vocabulary.example: A lack of confidence stood in the way of the goal.
collocations: stood in the way of your journey

questions.evidenceQuote: “What challenges or obstacles, such as a nemesis/rival or negative event, stood in the way of your journey?” “How did you personally grow as part of your journey to become who you are today?” “In what ways has your journey left a legacy?” These are the prompts that presumably lead a person to think of themselves as the hero of their story.

questions.prompt: What kind of growth is the journey prompt asking about?
questions.promptZh: 旅程提示询问哪种成长？
options: Only a measured increase in physical height.
Only the researcher's economic growth forecast.
A guarantee that every participant has already achieved all goals.
Personal development during the journey towards becoming one's present self.
optionsZh: 只问实测身高增长。
只问研究者经济增长预测。
保证每个参与者已完成全部目标。
在成为当下自己的历程中的个人发展。
analyses: A personally grow在身份旅程语境，不仅身体变高。
B 不是经济产出。
C 问how不证明每个目标已实现，也未提供全体结果保证。
D as part of journey、become who you are today把成长连到个人发展历程。

vocabulary.meaning: 个人成长；在理解、能力或自我认同方面发展
vocabulary.context: 不是只长高或赚更多钱，也不要求发展没有挫折。
vocabulary.example: She reflected on how she had personally grown through the experience.

questions.evidenceQuote: “What challenges or obstacles, such as a nemesis/rival or negative event, stood in the way of your journey?” “How did you personally grow as part of your journey to become who you are today?” “In what ways has your journey left a legacy?” These are the prompts that presumably lead a person to think of themselves as the hero of their story.

questions.prompt: What does 'left a legacy' mean in this journey question?
questions.promptZh: 旅程问题中的 left a legacy 是什么意思？
options: Only that the person has already written a legally valid inheritance document.
That the journey may have left a lasting contribution or influence.
That every participant must have founded a political dynasty.
That no effects of the journey remain at all.
optionsZh: 仅说此人已写好有效遗嘱。
这段历程可能留下持续的贡献或影响。
每位参与者必须建立政治世家。
历程完全没留下任何影响。
analyses: A legacy在这里不限法律遗产或遗嘱。
B 作为hero journey提示，要求反思留下的影响，不预先替每人编造伟大成就。
C 持久影响不要求政治世家，且无must。
D left a legacy的方向与毫无残留影响相反；提示问题不独自证明某位参与者已作特定贡献。

vocabulary.meaning: 留下的影响或贡献；遗产（广义）
vocabulary.context: 此处在旅程叙事中不限钱财或正式继承文件。
vocabulary.example: The project left a legacy of cooperation in the community.

questions.evidenceQuote: “What challenges or obstacles, such as a nemesis/rival or negative event, stood in the way of your journey?” “How did you personally grow as part of your journey to become who you are today?” “In what ways has your journey left a legacy?” These are the prompts that presumably lead a person to think of themselves as the hero of their story.

questions.prompt: How did the other half's questions differ from the journey prompts?
questions.promptZh: 另一半参与者的问题与旅程式提示有何区别？
options: They received the same heroic obstacles-and-legacy prompts with no change.
They were asked only about laboratory sticker donations.
They were asked more mundane questions about life features such as work and home.
They were given no questions and excluded from the story study entirely.
optionsZh: 他们收到同样英雄障碍与影响提示，完全无差异。
只问实验室贴纸捐赠。
他们被问较平常的生活特征，例如工作和住家。
他们完全不被提问，也被排除在故事研究外。
analyses: A other half与mundane说明对照，不是完全同提示。
B 属另一章研究。
C 原句具体列work and home，为相较英雄旅程的日常描述。
D were asked明确仍有提问，不是退出研究。

vocabulary.meaning: 平常的；日常而不特别戏剧化的
vocabulary.context: 用于问题风格对比，不自动贬低日常生活价值或诊断某人无趣。
vocabulary.example: The comparison group answered mundane questions about work and home.

questions.evidenceQuote: The other half of participants were asked a series of mundane questions such as, “Tell us various features of your life…such as your work and home.” Telling their stories as a hero made people feel that their lives were more meaningful and flourishing.

questions.prompt: What does the new section identify as key to a psychologically rich life?
questions.promptZh: 新一节指出心理丰富人生的关键是什么？
options: Memory.
Only a higher income.
Deleting every difficult event before telling a story.
Forgetting all past experiences as quickly as possible.
optionsZh: 记忆。
仅较高收入。
讲故事前删掉所有困难事件。
尽快忘掉所有过往经历。
analyses: A Memory is key直接给出主题，后句说明忘事会错过累积经历的机会。
B psychological wealth是经历积累的比喻，不是本句只讲收入。
C 前文并不建议抹去所有坏经历，本句也没有这个要求。
D forget...miss out是代价说明，非鼓励尽快遗忘。

vocabulary.meaning: 关键的；至关重要的因素
vocabulary.context: 在is key to中表示重要作用，不是门钥匙或只要记住就保证人生每维度完满。
vocabulary.example: Memory is key to preserving the value of an experience.

questions.evidenceQuote: Memory is key to a psychologically rich life.
